summary: The Illinois Department of Transportation noted that it was mutually agreed the School District would be compensated for trees and shrubs rather than including landscaping in the contract plans, and summarized the subsequent review process leading to the BOR's November 1974 letter deferring the recreation significance determination to the Park District for Chicago Heights.
text:
a.) It has been mutually agreed that the School District be compensated for the replacement of trees and shrubs rather than being included in the contract plans. If landscaping were included in the contract, the property would be affected by requiring a temporary easement to enter onto the property to do the contract items.

During the preparation of the Final Statement a review of the status of the Roosevelt School property involvement was conducted by the Board of Education, District No. 170 (See page G-7). Based upon this determination the U.S. Department of Interior - Bureau of Outdoor Recreation was requested to give opinion that the use of the Roosevelt School no longer constituted a Section 4(f) involvement. In a letter dated November 7, 1974, the United States Department of the Interior stated that the proper person to make a determination of recreation significance would be the Directr of the Park District for Chicago Heights. (See page G-5 and Chapter III, page III-7 for the present status)
